fatal_errors: The proposed aluminum alloy does not match the equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals investigated in the target study.
The proposed temperature range of -50 to 200 °C omits both the cryogenic inertial regime down to 9 K and most of the high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier regime extending to 1373 K.

The monotonic prediction that yield strength decreases with temperature misses the low-temperature CRSS increase and dulling, as well as the elevated-temperature CRSS peak and serrated flow caused by dynamic solute pinning.
No evidence is cited to support either the material selection or the asserted mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses temperature-dependent plasticity only at a generic level. It does not reconstruct the target materials, single-crystal compression geometry, CRSS measurement, strain-rate jumps, TEM/DFT analyses, or the composition-dependent MSAD, phonon-drag, and Cottrell-type pinning mechanisms. The proposed tensile experiment could test a simple aluminum trend, but it cannot discriminate the target study's inertial dulling, lattice-distortion scaling, or Portevin-Le Chatelier behavior. Its room-temperature baseline and stated scope are internally recognizable, yet too vague and unsupported to qualify as a well-supported alternative.
